STEP 1 - Scene: A snack-sized portion of cut cantaloupe pieces on a white square plate, photographed from directly overhead.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The square plate is about 22 cm across its diagonal-ish width, so the side is roughly 20 cm. Area is about 300 cm^2 (the corners are rounded and the shape is slightly irregular).

STEP 3 - Items: Cantaloupe (melon) chunks, about 9 pieces. There is no sauce or oil.

STEP 4 - Area: The pieces are roughly 3-4 cm long and 1.5-2 cm wide, about 4-5 cm^2 each. Nine pieces cover about 40 cm^2, which is about 13% of the plate. Total food coverage is about 13%.

STEP 5 - Volume: 40 cm^2 x about 1.3 cm thick = about 52 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Melon chunks are fairly dense, so I use a bulk density of about 0.65 g/ml. 52 x 0.65 = about 34 g. Measuring against the plate, individual pieces of about 4-6 g each would give 9 pieces = 45 g, so I settle on about 40 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Cantaloupe is about 34 kcal/100 g, so 40 g gives about 14 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A few melon pieces on a large plate weigh about 40 g and about 14 kcal, which is plausible.
